text:
The act of State doctrine means a domestic court will not judge the legality of a recognized foreign sovereign’s public acts performed inside that sovereign’s own territory. Those official acts are treated as valid, and challenges are left to diplomacy or the foreign state’s own legal system rather than domestic litigation. The doctrine is strongest in United States foreign-relations law (Underhill v. Hernandez; Banco Nacional de Cuba v. Sabbatino) and has a related, narrower form in English public law.
